summary.text: Fair-cheeked daughter of Ocean whom Aeetes, king of Colchis and son of Helios, took to wife by the will of the gods — and by her he begot neat-ankled Medea, the witch who would flee with Jason and the Golden Fleece.

story.text: Hesiod closes the Sun-born house with her marriage: Perseis daughter of Ocean bore Circe and Aeetes to Helios, and Aeetes in turn wedded Idyia, daughter of Ocean the perfect stream; through golden Aphrodite she was subject to him in love and bore neat-ankled Medea — the only child the Theogony names in this Colchian line.

Apollodorus knows her only as the mother behind the witch: when Jason came to Aeetes for the fleece and won it through Medea's drugs and counsel, the king learned what his daughter had done and pursued the Argo — while Medea, fleeing with Jason, would cast her brother Apsyrtus limb from limb into the deep for Aeetes to gather.

Apollonius sets her in Aeetes' palace: after the Caucasian nymph Asterodeia had borne him Apsyrtus, the king took Eidyia, youngest daughter of Tethys and Oceanus, as his wedded wife, and his daughters were Chalciope and Medea — Medea, who spent her days in Hecate's temple as the goddess's priestess.
